steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our paper presenting a V2X cooperative perception dataset: motivate cooperative perception with roadside sensors and V2X, explain why such datasets are needed, and list our contributions.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
- Advantages of cooperative perception (onboard + roadside sensors)
- Sharing infrastructure perception via V2X
- Intelligent Transportation Systems and the need for V2X datasets
- Contributions

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
- Cooperative perception
  - fusion of onboard + roadside sensor data; enhances autonomous vehicles, road safety
  - multiple sources: robust to sensor failures, adverse environmental conditions
  - roadside sensors: elevated view, detect obstacles early
  - precise vehicle localization; offload perception tasks -> less computational load on automated vehicles
  - global perspective of traffic, comprehensive situational awareness when fused with onboard data
  - fewer false positives/negatives via cross-validation of sensors
- V2X
  - infrastructure shares perception info with vehicles via V2X
  - minimal delay, real-time -> better situational awareness and decision-making
- ITS + need for datasets
  - ITS, e.g. Testbed for Autonomous Driving (cite): safety via real-time traffic info
  - testbeds increasingly use LiDAR -> accurate live digital twin of traffic (cite)
  - connected vehicles: far-reaching view, react early to breakdowns/accidents
  - lane and speed recommendations -> traffic flow
  - ego-centric datasets: many occlusions, e.g. large truck in front of ego vehicle
  - roadside sensors at smart intersection: broad overview, full-surround view
  - specific need for V2X datasets; high cost of collecting/labeling; step toward large-scale ITS
- Contributions
  - V2X dataset for cooperative 3D object detection and tracking: 2,000 labeled point clouds, 5,000 labeled images, 30k 3D boxes with track IDs; near-miss, overtaking, U-turn, traffic violations
  - open-source 3D BAT v24.3.2 annotation tool for multi-modal V2X labeling
  - CoopDet3D cooperative 3D detection model; beats single view models by +14.3 3D mAP; extensive experiments, ablations
  - development kit: load annotations in OpenLABEL standard format (cite); preprocess, visualize, convert labels between formats, evaluate perception and tracking

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Cooperative perception means fusing the data from onboard sensors with data from roadside sensors, and it has several advantages for making autonomous vehicles more capable and improving road safety. When data from multiple sources is used, the perception becomes more robust to sensor failures or bad environmental conditions. The roadside sensors have an elevated view that helps to detect obstacles early. They also help with precise vehicle localization, and they reduce the computational load of automated vehicles because some perception tasks can be offloaded to the roadside sensors. Roadside sensors give a global perspective of the traffic and when they are fused with onboard sensor data they offer comprehensive situational awareness. There are also fewer false positives or negatives, because cooperative perception cross-validates the information coming from different sensors.

The infrastructure sensors can share information related to perception with the vehicles through V2X. Because of the minimal delay and real-time capabilities, the perception systems based on infrastructure can further enhance the situational awareness and the decision-making processes of the vehicles.

- ITS + need for datasets
  - ITS, e.g. Testbed for Autonomous Driving (cite): safety via real-time traffic info
  - testbeds increasingly use LiDAR -> accurate live digital twin of traffic (cite)
  - connected vehicles: far-reaching view, react early to breakdowns/accidents
  - lane and speed recommendations -> traffic flow
  - ego-centric datasets: many occlusions, e.g. large truck in front of ego vehicle
  - roadside sensors at smart intersection: broad overview, full-surround view
  - specific need for V2X datasets; high cost of collecting/labeling; step toward large-scale ITS
- Contributions
  - V2X dataset for cooperative 3D object detection and tracking: 2,000 labeled point clouds, 5,000 labeled images, 30k 3D boxes with track IDs; near-miss, overtaking, U-turn, traffic violations
  - open-source 3D BAT v24.3.2 annotation tool for multi-modal V2X labeling
  - CoopDet3D cooperative 3D detection model; beats single view models by +14.3 3D mAP; extensive experiments, ablations

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Cooperative perception means fusing the data from onboard sensors with data from roadside sensors, and it has several advantages for making autonomous vehicles more capable and improving road safety. When data from multiple sources is used, the perception becomes more robust to sensor failures or bad environmental conditions. The roadside sensors have an elevated view that helps to detect obstacles early. They also help with precise vehicle localization, and they reduce the computational load of automated vehicles because some perception tasks can be offloaded to the roadside sensors. Roadside sensors give a global perspective of the traffic and when they are fused with onboard sensor data they offer comprehensive situational awareness. There are also fewer false positives or negatives, because cooperative perception cross-validates the information coming from different sensors.

The infrastructure sensors can share information related to perception with the vehicles through V2X. Because of the minimal delay and real-time capabilities, the perception systems based on infrastructure can further enhance the situational awareness and the decision-making processes of the vehicles.

Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) such as the Testbed for Autonomous Driving want to improve safety by providing real-time traffic information. According to prior work, testbeds are starting to use LiDAR sensors extensively in their setups to create an accurate live digital twin of the traffic. Connected vehicles get a far-reaching view, so they can react to breakdowns or accidents early. ITS systems also give lane and speed recommendations to improve the traffic flow. The main challenge with ego-centric vehicle datasets is that there are many occlusions from the vehicle perspective, e.g., when a large truck in front of the ego vehicle blocks the view. Roadside sensors at a smart intersection give a broad overview of the intersection and a full-surround view. Because ITS has such big potential, there is a specific need for V2X datasets. Collecting and labeling such datasets is very costly, but this work addresses this challenge as an important step toward large-scale ITS implementations.

Our contributions are:

- We provide a high-quality V2X dataset for cooperative 3D object detection and tracking, with 2,000 labeled point clouds and 5,000 labeled images. In total 30k 3D bounding boxes with track IDs were labeled, in challenging traffic scenarios such as near-miss events, overtaking scenarios, U-turn maneuvers and traffic violation events.

- We open-source our 3D bounding box annotation tool (3D BAT v24.3.2) for labeling multi-modal V2X datasets.

- We propose CoopDet3D, a cooperative 3D object detection model, and we show in extensive experiments and ablation studies that it is better than single view models on our V2X dataset by +14.3 3D mAP.

- Finally, we provide a development kit that loads the annotations in OpenLABEL, which is a widely recognized standard format, so that the dataset can be integrated and used seamlessly. It can also preprocess, visualize and convert labels to and from different dataset formats, and evaluate perception and tracking methods.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Cooperative perception involves the fusion of onboard sensor data and roadside sensor data, and it offers several advantages for enhancing the capabilities of autonomous vehicles and improving road safety. Using data from multiple sources makes perception more robust to sensor failures or adverse environmental conditions. Roadside sensors provide an elevated view that helps to detect obstacles early. They are also beneficial for precise vehicle localization and reduce the computational load of automated vehicles by offloading some perception tasks to the roadside. Roadside sensors provide a global perspective of the traffic and offer comprehensive situational awareness when fused with onboard sensor data. Furthermore, there are fewer false positives or negatives because cooperative perception cross-validates the information from different sensors.

Infrastructure sensors can share perception-related information with vehicles through V2X. Due to minimal delay and real-time capabilities, infrastructure-based perception systems can further enhance the situational awareness and decision-making processes of vehicles.

Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) like the Testbed for Autonomous Driving [1] aim to improve safety by providing real-time traffic information. According to [2], testbeds are increasingly using LiDAR sensors in their setups to create an accurate live digital twin of the traffic. Connected vehicles get a far-reaching view, which enables them to react to breakdowns or accidents early. ITS systems also provide lane and speed recommendations to improve traffic flow. The key challenge with ego-centric vehicle datasets is that there are many occlusions from a vehicle perspective, e.g., when a large truck in front of the ego vehicle obscures the view. Roadside sensors located at a smart intersection, in contrast, provide a broad overview of the intersection and a full-surround view. Given the immense potential of ITS, there is a specific need for V2X datasets. Despite the high costs of collecting and labeling such datasets, this work addresses this challenge as a crucial step toward realizing large-scale ITS implementations.

Our contributions are as follows:

- We provide a high-quality V2X dataset for the cooperative 3D object detection and tracking task with 2,000 labeled point clouds and 5,000 labeled images. In total, 30k 3D bounding boxes with track IDs were labeled in challenging traffic scenarios like near-miss events, overtaking scenarios, U-turn maneuvers, and traffic violation events.

- We open-source our 3D bounding box annotation tool (3D BAT v24.3.2) for labeling multi-modal V2X datasets.

- We propose CoopDet3D, a cooperative 3D object detection model, and show in extensive experiments and ablation studies that it outperforms single view models on our V2X dataset by +14.3 3D mAP.

- Finally, we provide a development kit to load the annotations in the widely recognized standard format OpenLABEL [3], to facilitate seamless integration and utilization of the dataset. It can also preprocess, visualize, and convert labels to and from different dataset formats, and evaluate perception and tracking methods.

References:
[1] Annkathrin Krämmer, Christoph Schöller, Dhiraj Gulati, Venkatnarayanan Lakshminarasimhan, Franz Kurz, Dominik Rosenbaum, Claus Lenz, and Alois Knoll. Providentia-a large-scale sensor system for the assistance of autonomous vehicles and its evaluation. Journal of Field Robotics , pages 1156–1176, 2022.
[2] Christian Creß, Zhenshan Bing, and Alois C. Knoll. Intelligent transportation systems using external infrastructure: A literature survey. https://arxiv.org/pdf/2112.05615 .
[3] Nicco Hagedorn. OpenLABEL Concept Paper.
